topics.label: Course introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: These remarks introduce the lecturer, the module context, and the lecture's core learning objectives.

topics.label: Principles of cancer causation, risk factors, and epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental drivers of cancer development, spanning genetic mutations, environmental risk, stochastic bad luck, and global epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how oncogenic bacteria, parasites, and viruses contribute to malignant transformation, illustrated through Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and DNA damage mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the biochemical mechanisms by which dietary toxins, radiation, and chemical carcinogens undergo metabolic activation and induce DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, host susceptibility, and mechanisms of carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic tumor promotion, inflammatory microenvironments, developmental windows of host susceptibility, and summarize these carcinogenic mechanisms.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying carcinogens and assessing cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro approaches used to identify carcinogens and evaluate cancer risk against benefits.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a final recap of key themes and closing remarks.
